items.note: Two Excel blocks stacked in one picture: an INPUTS block of seven labelled rows with two degree columns, and a Probabilities block of six numbered rows against the three standard-deviation columns. Same family in both panels, so one row with a panel count of two [geometry.panel_count].

note:
Paper 78, Team 39173, a 2015 paper that builds a probability-of-containment model for a missing transoceanic flight and then runs it on Flight ABCD from Boston to Lisbon. Eighteen measured regions over fourteen of the thirty-two pages, every one of them an exhibit: eighteen figure rows, no refusal, no printed table and nothing unresolved. The paper prints thirteen numbered figures and all thirteen own a region; the other five rows are unnumbered pictures that carry no caption at all.

What the exhibits are. Three drawings carry the geometry of the model - the search cone of Figure 1, the SAN x 6 matrix of Figure 2 and the single referenced cell of Figure 3 - and eight line plots carry the sensitivity sweep of Figures 4 to 8 and the two search paths of Figures 12 and 13. One surface, Figure 9, is the joint density the whole method integrates; one 3-D bar chart, Figure 10, is the discretised result; and four blocks are preserved tables. The five unnumbered pictures are the route map on p16, the density curve on p17 and the three Excel screenshots of pp23 and 26.

The one caption that does not match its picture is Figure 11. The printed caption reads 'Map representation of POC allocated to each of the search regions', which is what a reader would expect next to the 3-D bar chart above it, but the pixels are a ruled seven-column table titled 'Probability of Containment for Search Regions'. The record keeps the caption as printed and classifies the picture as table-as-figure rather than repairing either side.

The worked example sits inside the region pass's blind spot. Section 3's heading is set at the very foot of p16, printed with its folio caught in the same line, and the heading index never sees it: it reads pp17-22 as 2.6.2 Weaknesses, which would file the joint density, the discretised POC, the allocation table and both search paths under a weaknesses paragraph. The 2.1.2 heading is missed too, so Figure 3 would inherit 2.1.1. Every path in this record was typed from the printed headings and the contents page.

Caption and citation are both thin. Figure 7 stops mid-condition, Figure 1's censored fraction reaches the layer as spaced digits, and the two search-path captions are hyphenated mid-word. Ten of the thirteen numbered figures are never named in prose; the three that are get a single bare pointer each, and all three point backwards - Figure 1 from ten pages later. Not one sentence in the paper forecasts an exhibit.
rules: Families split six ways over eighteen rows: eight line plots, four table-as-figure blocks, three flowchart-or-schematic drawings, one map-or-plan-view frame, one surface-or-3D and one bar [geometry.family].

The four table-as-figure rows are all preserved tables rather than drawn plots - three spreadsheet screenshots from the appendices and Figure 11, whose printed caption calls it a map representation while the picture is a seven-column probability table [geometry.family].
Only one row is a 3-D rendering with bars, Figure 10, and it is recorded with three_d perspective-bars rather than with the surface rows [geometry.three_d].

Two rows carry more than one panel and neither is a composite: the stacked INPUTS and Probabilities blocks on p26 are the same family twice, so one row with a panel count of two [geometry.panel_count].
Every caption in the paper prints BELOW its artwork, the thirteen numbered ones alike [caption.position].

Numbering is 'Figure N:' for the thirteen printed figures and 'none' for the five pictures that never receive a number - the route map on p16, the density curve on p17, and the three spreadsheet blocks on pp23 and 26 [caption.numbering].

Caption fidelity is poor. Figure 7's caption stops mid-condition at 'where 0 <= hs <' with no bound, the glyph reaching the layer as a control character; Figure 1's censored fraction reaches the layer as spaced digits; Figure 12 and Figure 13 are hyphenated mid-word in their own subtitles. Each verbatim stops where the printed caption stops [caption.verbatim].

Citation is the weakest part of the paper: ten of the thirteen numbered figures are never named in the prose at all. Figure 1 is named once on p16, ten pages after it prints; Figure 4 once on p14, a page after it prints; Figure 11 once on p20, a page after it prints. Figures 12 and 13 are referred to only as 'the two figures above' [mention.count].
Every one of the three named exhibits is cited after it prints - leads of -10, -1 and -1 - so not one clause in the paper forecasts an exhibit [mention.lead_pages].

Section paths are rebuilt by hand. The heading index never returns section 3 - its title sits at the foot of p16 after the weaknesses prose, and the index reads pp17-22 as 2.6.2 Weaknesses - and it never returns 2.1.2, so the Figure 3 row would inherit 2.1.1. The path behind 3 Working Example is checked against the layer [place.section_path].

Area separates the row kinds here: the smallest row is the Shifted Coords block at 14.6 percent of the measure and the largest is the search-region matrix at 53.5 percent, a factor of six between them [place.area_frac].

Nothing in this paper is a printed table with a number, so the table list is empty; the word Table never once appears in the text layer, which is why the three spreadsheet blocks are figure rows [geometry.family].
